headline: Coast Guard suspends search for six aboard medical plane off Nantucket
dek: The Coast Guard ended its active search after 66 hours and more than 4,400 square miles of ocean were covered; the six people aboard remain unaccounted for and an investigation is expected.
body: The U.S. Coast Guard suspended its active search Sunday for the six people aboard a medical transport jet that disappeared on a Bermuda-to-Boston flight. The decision came after about 66 hours of operations covering more than 4,400 square miles of ocean, according to the [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/plane-search-bermuda-boston-nantucket-35f4da84247adcc4d91e0e7e81b3d26e). A debris field found off Nantucket had already been confirmed as belonging to the aircraft. The people aboard remain unaccounted for, and authorities have not released a final casualty determination.

Rear Adm. Matthew Lake, commander of the Coast Guard’s Northeast District, said suspending the search was not an easy decision and expressed condolences to the families and loved ones affected, AP reported. The Coast Guard’s statement also thanked partner agencies that helped with the response. The suspension ends the active rescue phase described in earlier reports, but it does not establish the cause of the incident or answer what happened to each person aboard.

The aircraft was a Canadian-registered Gulfstream G100 operated by Latitude Air Ambulance. It left L.F. Wade International Airport in Bermuda for Boston Logan International Airport with four Canadian crew members and two Bermudian passengers, a patient and the patient’s companion, according to the [Royal Gazette](https://www.royalgazette.com/general/news/article/20261005/search-launched-for-missing-air-ambulance/). The Coast Guard’s Northeast District identified the flight in an [official update](https://x.com/USCGNortheast/status/2106332164568801317). The Federal Aviation Administration reported losing contact with the plane early Saturday, shortly before its expected arrival in Boston.

The debris field was located roughly 20 miles off Nantucket in water about 80 to 90 feet deep, the Royal Gazette reported after a Coast Guard briefing. The field was described as extensive, making it difficult for crews to determine immediately what evidence it contained. Families of those aboard were notified as the search progressed, but officials have not publicly identified the six people. The Coast Guard said a future investigation into the circumstances would be coordinated by the appropriate investigative authorities.

The response brought together Coast Guard aircraft, boats and cutters, Massachusetts authorities and the New York National Guard’s Air Rescue Wing. [Boston 25 News](https://www.boston25news.com/news/local/coast-guard-suspends-search-missing-medical-transfer-jet-found-off-nantucket/I4YKQH5TABGGDNWHKKDC73YEYA/?outputType=amp) reported that the search included assets from Air Station Cape Cod, Station Brant Point and the cutter William Sparling. AP reported that crews used fixed-wing aircraft, helicopters, boats and cutters while searching the large area south of Nantucket.

The aircraft’s final moments remain preliminary evidence, not a finding about the cause. Air-traffic-control audio reviewed by Boston 25 and AP included a controller asking whether the pilot was “coming in blind.” The pilot had reported electrical problems and declared an emergency, according to the audio reports, but the response was not audible. Preliminary flight-tracking data showed a sharp drop from roughly 24,000 feet to between 10,000 and 11,000 feet. Those details do not by themselves establish whether equipment failure, weather or another factor caused the loss of contact.

The National Transportation Safety Board told AP it was gathering information, while Canadian and Bermudian officials remained in contact with families and U.S. authorities. The next phase will focus on the debris, any recoverable aircraft evidence and the formal investigation rather than an active search for survivors on the surface. Nantucket and Cape Cod were central to the response because the debris was found near the island and the Boston-bound flight was approaching the region when contact was lost.

The confirmed picture is therefore limited but significant: a Canadian medical flight disappeared near Nantucket, crews found debris associated with it, six people remain unaccounted for, and the Coast Guard has suspended active search operations after an extensive regional effort. The identities of those aboard, the full crash sequence and the cause remain unresolved. NorthEast News will treat flight audio, tracking data and commentary about possible causes as preliminary until investigators issue verified findings.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Coast Guard suspends Nantucket medical plane search
seoDescription: The Coast Guard suspended its search after 66 hours for six people aboard a medical plane that vanished near Nantucket.
